mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.2% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.2% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals economic weakness that reduces consumer spending and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A joint condition of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0) and declining interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.2%) indicates central bank response to inflation with rate cuts, supporting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the joint signal is negative over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a supply contraction regime (INDPRO < 90.0), a rise in housing starts (HOUST > 550) signals improving construction activity and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 90.0 and HOUST > 550 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts index above 500 indicates strengthening consumer demand for housing, correlating with positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when HOUST > 500 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts index below 500 signals weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 500 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in employment (PAYEMS > 130000) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE < 10.0%) indicates labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS > 130000 and UNRATE < 10.0) yields negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 218.5 indicates elevated inflation that triggers expectations of monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 218.5 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
